cast_path: torch.Tensor.to(torch.float16) direct from bfloat16 (no fp32 intermediate in the stored result; fp32 used only for measurement)

cast_exactness.explanation: BF16 has an 8-bit significand (1 implicit + 7 explicit); FP16 has an 11-bit significand (1 implicit + 10 explicit). For any BF16 value whose magnitude lies in the FP16 normal range [6.103515625e-5, 65504], the FP16 significand is a strict superset of the BF16 significand, so the cast is EXACT (bit-for-bit equal value, max_abs_diff 0) — verified by measurement. The cast is NOT exact only where the value is outside that magnitude window: (a) overflow, |x| > 65504, which FP16 cannot represent finitely (becomes inf); (b) subnormal window [5.96e-8, 6.103515625e-5), where FP16 subnormals lose significand bits at the LOW end (a subnormal has fewer effective significand bits as it shrinks), so some BF16 values round to a different (subnormal) FP16 value or to 0; (c) underflow, 0 < |x| < 5.960464477539063e-8, which rounds to 0. Note the asymmetry: overflow loses the value (inf), subnormal rounding loses low-order mantissa bits (representability gap), underflow to zero loses the value entirely.
